newsitem.title: USA: Calif. Senate OKs bill to merge bonding agencies.
newsitem.headline: Calif. Senate OKs bill to merge bonding agencies.

text.p: California's Senate approved a bill Thursday that would consolidate two state bonding authorities under the state Trade and Commerce Agency.
The Senate approved the bill on a vote of 36-0, sending it to the Assembly for review.

The bill by Senator Mike Thompson would merge the California Infrastructure and Economic Development Bank and the California Economic Development Financing Authority into a single entity within the state's Trade and Commerce Agency.
Thompson, a Democrat, said the bill would establish a "one-stop shop" for dealing with California's public and private infrastructure needs.
A separate bill by Thompson would put a $200 million bond on the ballot to provide capital for infrastructure projects. The bond bill is still pending in the Senate.
